flaws.title: Downward reset scans bitmap words without stopping at endTick, so taxed zero-for-one swaps can run out of gas
flaws.sequence:
1. The pool is in a state with no initialized tick at or below the current tick. This happens when all positions lie above the price, for example after the price has left every range or when LPs only provide one-sided liquidity above the price. It also happens when the nearest initialized tick below is many bitmap words away.
2. A user sends a top-of-block zero-for-one swap with a non-zero priority fee, so taxInEther > 0.
3. afterSwap calls _zeroForOneDistributeTax, which calls initDown and then reset(slot0BeforeSwap.tick()).
4. reset finds no initialized bit in the start word. It then decrements wordPos and calls getPoolBitmapInfo (an extsload) for every word until it finds an initialized bit or reaches wordPos == type(int16).min. It never checks whether it has already passed self.endTick.
5. That can mean tens of thousands of cold external storage reads, and the hook then calls reset a second time. The gas cost exceeds the block gas limit and the whole swap reverts.
flaws.impact: Taxed (top-of-block) zero-for-one swaps revert whenever the bitmap below the start tick is sparse or empty. The upward iterator stops at endTick, so this affects only the downward path. Users cannot swap in this direction with a priority fee, the MEV tax cannot be collected or distributed to LPs, and the pool's top-of-block path is blocked until liquidity appears below the price.

requirement_breaks: The initial scan in reset is not bounded by self.endTick. Unlike the upward iterator and _advanceToNextDown, it keeps loading bitmap words far below the end of the walk. This wastes gas and can make the call fail even though the returned tick set is logically correct.
